text:
alex: heads-up — i'm doing a tiny spike on abort paths for the eviction/handoff fastpath. hit a case where we assign the lease but an abort leaves a dangling lease and readers can see stale state :confused:

maria: can you sketch the sequence that triggers it?

alex: simplified sequence:
1) pin prefix A
2) assign lease to node B (fastpath)
3) attempt owner swap (atomic step)
4) crash/abort between 2 and 3 => lease exists on B but ownership not flipped

josh: hmm, so requests after that might hit the lease on B and think they're the owner but the sequencer hasn't moved ownership?

alex: exactly. observed a read that returned stale cached kv because the sequencer still considered A owned by old node. replicates under tight race and prefills.

tia: do we currently have an abort handler that clears the lease? i thought we did a best-effort revoke on failure.

maria: we do best-effort, but best-effort isn't synchronous and can be lost on process crash. needs durable state somewhere. :thinking:

alex: proposed mitigations:
- add an explicit "handoff_state" metadata on prefix: {idle,in_flight,aborted} (small enum) so readers treat in_flight as not-owned and fallback to prefetch
- on abort, mark aborted + emit metric and durable event so crash-recovery can drive cleanup
- short TTL tombstone to prevent immediate reassign until cleanup finishes

josh: i like the read-side defensive check: if lease exists but sequencer ownership != lease.owner then treat as miss. cheap and local.

tia: downside: extra royalty on read path (one extra ownership lookup) but we already do a few lookups. maybe make it opt-in behind a feature flag for canary.

maria: telemetry question: we should emit a distinct counter `evict.handoff.abort` with labels (prefix, attempted_owner, reason) and a histogram for time-to-recover so we can measure impact. also surface in console.

alex: agreed. i'll add counters. also thinking about making abort idempotent: write an abort-record to prefix txn log so recovery pass can see incomplete handoffs and reconcile.

josh: careful with txn log growth. maybe compact abort records into prefix's last_handoff_epoch field. recovery scans last_handoff_epoch vs active leases.

tia: practical rollout approach:
1) read-side invariant change (if lease.owner != seq.owner treat as miss) behind a flag
2) emit abort metrics in fastpath
3) add handoff_state metadata and abort-write path (canary small pool)
4) add recovery pass to reconcile stale leases using last_handoff_epoch

alex: plan sounds good. i'll open a short RFC + checklist. quick patch for step 1 would be valuable to reduce impact now.

maria: i'll take telemetry + console wiring. i'll also add an alert if abort rate spikes > 1/m for a pool.

josh: i'll prototype the `lease vs seq owner` check and run it through our hotpath perf test.

tia: i'll own rollout automation and the canary gate.

deploy-bot: canary job queued: `kv-evict-abort-check-canary` (jobs/1248) :rocket:

alex: thanks all — i'll post the RFC link when ready and add a minimal unit test to reproduce the race. want to catch any other edgecases i missed.

maria: maybe also note cross-shard transfers — same invariant but extra messaging hop. call it out in RFC.

alex: good call. will add. :thumbsup:
